title: Dynamic Planet: Earth's Fresh Waters
summary: Follow water from rainfall through a drainage basin to the sea and into the ground, and read a river's history from the landforms it leaves and the data it generates.
objectives: Account for water quantitatively through a cycle, a budget and a reservoir residence time.
Read a drainage basin from a map: divides, stream order, drainage pattern and density.
Explain a channel's form and landforms from the sediment and discharge that made them.
Interpret hydrographs, longitudinal profiles, flood-frequency plots and grain-size data.
Trace groundwater through aquifers and karst, and predict how pumping and land use change it.

units.title: Accounting for Water
units.summary: Every question about fresh water is finally a bookkeeping question: what comes in, what leaves, and what is stored in between.
objectives: Name the fluxes of the hydrologic cycle and say which direction each moves water.
Compute a water budget and a reservoir residence time.

lessons.title: The Hydrologic Cycle and Its Fluxes
lessons.objective: Trace water through precipitation, evaporation, evapotranspiration, infiltration and runoff, and state which flux dominates in a given setting.

lessons.title: Reservoirs, Residence Time, and Water Budgets
lessons.objective: Compute a residence time from storage and flux, and balance a water budget for a basin or lake.

units.title: Where Fresh Water Falls
units.summary: Climate decides how much water a landscape ever gets, and topography decides where it lands.
objectives: Predict precipitation from topography and position on a continent.
Place a landscape on the arid-to-humid spectrum from its streams and deposits.

lessons.title: Climatic and Topographic Controls on Precipitation
lessons.objective: Explain orographic lift, rain shadow, continentality and lake effect, and use them to predict which side of a range is wet.

lessons.title: Arid, Semiarid, and Humid Landscapes
lessons.objective: Read a climate regime from perennial versus ephemeral streams, playas and evaporite deposits.

units.title: Reading a Drainage Basin
units.summary: A watershed is the unit of this event: learn to see one on a map and most map questions become answerable.
objectives: Trace a drainage divide and delineate a basin on a topographic map.
Assign stream order and name a drainage pattern from network geometry.

lessons.title: Watersheds, Divides, and Basin Characteristics
lessons.objective: Delineate a drainage basin from contours and describe its shape, relief and area.

lessons.title: Stream Order, Drainage Patterns, and Density
lessons.objective: Assign Strahler stream order and infer bedrock and structure from dendritic, trellis, radial and rectangular patterns.

units.title: Streamflow and Floods
units.summary: Discharge is the number that drives a river's behaviour, and the hydrograph is how it is read.
objectives: Compute discharge and relate velocity, area and load.
Read a hydrograph and interpret a recurrence interval honestly.

lessons.title: Discharge, Velocity, and the Hydrograph
lessons.objective: Compute discharge from cross-sectional area and velocity, and read rising limb, peak, lag and baseflow from a hydrograph.

lessons.title: Floods, Frequency, and Recurrence Intervals
lessons.objective: Interpret a recurrence interval as a probability, and explain why a 100-year flood can occur twice in a decade.

units.title: Sediment and Channel Form
units.summary: A channel's shape is the visible result of the sediment and water moving through it.
objectives: Classify sediment by size, sorting and rounding and infer its transport history.
Explain a channel planform from slope, discharge and sediment supply.

lessons.title: Sediment Properties and How Rivers Move Them
lessons.objective: Distinguish bed, suspended and dissolved load, and separate competence from capacity using a grain-size and velocity relationship.

lessons.title: Channel Planform, Sinuosity, and Bedforms
lessons.objective: Classify a channel as braided, meandering, straight or anastomosing, calculate sinuosity, and identify ripples, dunes, antidunes and bars.

units.title: Rivers as Sculptors
units.summary: Given a landform, name the process that made it — this is where most points in a fluvial event live.
objectives: Relate the longitudinal profile to base level and dynamic equilibrium.
Identify erosional and depositional landforms and the process behind each.

lessons.title: Longitudinal Profile, Base Level, and Graded Streams
lessons.objective: Explain gradient and base level, and predict a stream's response to a change in either using dynamic equilibrium.

lessons.title: Floodplain and Channel Landforms
lessons.objective: Identify point bars, cut banks, oxbow lakes, natural levees, deltas and alluvial fans, and state the process that forms each.

units.title: Water Underground
units.summary: Most liquid fresh water is below the surface, and it obeys rules a surface-water intuition gets wrong.
objectives: Locate the water table and classify an aquifer.
Predict groundwater flow and the effects of pumping and recharge change.

lessons.title: The Water Table and Aquifer Types
lessons.objective: Distinguish the zones of aeration and saturation, and classify confined, unconfined and artesian aquifers by porosity and permeability.

lessons.title: Groundwater Flow and Its Link to Rivers
lessons.objective: Use hydraulic gradient to predict flow direction, and explain gaining and losing streams, recharge, cones of depression and saltwater intrusion.

lessons.title: Karst: Landscapes Made by Dissolution
lessons.objective: Explain carbonate dissolution and identify sinkholes, caves, disappearing streams, springs and solution valleys.

units.title: Lakes, Wetlands, and Human Hands
units.summary: Standing water stratifies and turns over on a schedule, and almost every basin now also has people in it.
objectives: Explain lake stratification and seasonal turnover.
Predict how dams, levees, channelization and pumping change a basin.

lessons.title: Lakes, Stratification, and Turnover
lessons.objective: Explain how a lake forms, balance its budget, and describe thermal stratification and spring and fall turnover.

lessons.title: Wetlands and Lake Shorelines
lessons.objective: Distinguish bogs, marshes, swamps and fens, and describe the processes shaping a lake shoreline.

lessons.title: Human Impacts on Fresh Water
lessons.objective: Predict the downstream and subsurface consequences of dams, levees, channelization, land-use change and groundwater pumping.

units.title: Competition Application
units.summary: The event is half data interpretation, so the last skill is reading the displays a supervisor will actually hand you.
objectives: Extract an answer from a topographic map, hydrograph, profile or grain-size plot.
Structure a station answer so partial credit is earned under time pressure.

lessons.title: Reading Maps, Hydrographs, and Cross-Sections
lessons.objective: Work a mixed set of freshwater data displays and justify each answer from the evidence shown.

lessons.title: Station Strategy and Earning Partial Credit
lessons.objective: Budget time across stations and write answers that earn the reasoning points even when the identification is uncertain.
